title: ID0453797-DC/Si-D/CZ-[MP / R7 170002211] Power converter issue
description:
Reported behavior/issue - Power converter issue
Solution:
Following the procedure for diagnosing a power converter issue, and after our check, as shown in the screenshot I sent, we can see that converter number 13 is faulty.
There are three possible solutions:
First, check the AC-DC cables attached to that converter. If they are properly connected, proceed to the next step.
Try swapping the converter that shows the issue with the one beside it. This will help confirm whether the problem lies in the cables or in the converter itself. If the issue remains after swapping, it confirms that the converter itself is faulty. In that case, replace the converter.

additional_info.subject: RE: ID0453797-DC/Si-D/CZ-[MP / R7 170002211] Power converter issue CRM:03042000012
additional_info.body:
Dear Younes,
When on site, we powercycled the charger, but the problem on converter 2102312VGQKXNB000226SA042200000204FW prevailed.
Then we replaced it with an adjacent converter, and the fault moved with the converter itself. Therefore, we can rule out a communication problem.
In the meantime new converter came to fault state.
@Gaspar Martins, Laura (SI E CS SD ES)
was mentioning in the ticket ID0453780  that the new FW release should tackle these issues?
Do you recommend us to order new power converters and replace the units, or to wait for the FW release and see it solves the problem?
Thank you for your support here.
Kind regards,
Milan

additional_info.subject: ID0453797-DC/Si-D/CZ-[MP / R7 170002211] Power converter issue CRM:03042000012

Hi Milan,
The idea was to go to site and replace the converter if the swap didn't work.
The FW update might or not work, we don't know 100%, so the idea here is, if there is a problem that needs to be fixed now, then replace as per the instructions previously shared.
Thank you!
Best regards,
Francisco
